01

Setting specification

Task

Return a feasible primal–dual pair for the constrained minimax problem with small game-stationarity residual. Stationarity is tested separately for minimizing in the first block and maximizing in the second block.

Solve $\min_{x\in X}\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$.

Admissible model

The set $X$ is known, nonempty, closed, and convex. The set $Y$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(Y)\le D_y$.

The function $f$ is jointly $\beta$-smooth on $X\times Y$. For every $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is concave. Convexity in the $x$ direction and a positive strong-concavity modulus are not required.

The public feasible initial point $(x_0,y_0)$ satisfies $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_{x\in X}\Phi(x)\le\Delta<\infty$, where $\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$.

Oracle interface

Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $D_y$, $\Delta$, $\beta$, and $\varepsilon$, together with the stated initial points and feasible-set information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.

$$ (x,y)\longmapsto(f(x,y),\nabla_xf(x,y),\nabla_yf(x,y)) $$

Queries satisfy $(x,y)\in X\times Y$. The exact value and both gradient blocks form one bundled response.

Exact Euclidean projection onto the known set is allowed. Its calls are recorded separately and excluded from the primary query count.

Output

Return a feasible pair $(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in X\times Y$.

The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Compute the constrained stationarity residual for each block, using the payoff gradient in the minimizing block and its negative in the maximizing block. Accuracy is the larger of those residuals and must be at most $\varepsilon$.

$$ \max\{\operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla_xf(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})+N_X(\widehat{x})),\operatorname{dist}(0,-\nabla_yf(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})+N_Y(\widehat{y}))\} $$

For a closed convex set $K$, define $N_K(z)=\{v:\langle v,u-z\rangle\le0,\ \forall u\in K\}$ for $z\in K$, and $\operatorname{dist}(0,S)=\inf_{v\in S}\|v\|_2$.

Resource accounting

Each bundled value-and-joint-gradient call counts once in $N_{\rm first}$. Projection counts are recorded separately.

Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Any measurable sequential adaptive deterministic algorithm is allowed. Queries and outputs may use the complete history, with no additional span, zero-support, communication, or memory restriction.

The same deterministic algorithm must satisfy the guarantee for every admissible instance.

$$ \max\{\operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla_xf(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})+N_X(\widehat{x})),\operatorname{dist}(0,-\nabla_yf(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})+N_Y(\widehat{y}))\}\le\varepsilon. $$

Budget convention
fixed_worst_case_cap
02

Notation and parameters

$A$

The dimensionless scale of the initial primal objective gap.

Domain
Positive real number

$A=\beta\Delta/\varepsilon^2$

$B$

The dimensionless scale of the dual-domain diameter.

Domain
A nonnegative real.

$B=\beta D_y/\varepsilon$

$D_y$

Euclidean diameter bound for the dual feasible domain

Domain
A nonnegative real.

$\operatorname{diam}(Y)=\sup_{u,v\in Y}\|u-v\|_2\le D_y$

$\Delta$

A public bound on the initial reduced-objective value above its infimum. Attainment of the infimum is not required.

Domain
Positive real number

$\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$

$\beta$

Euclidean Lipschitz upper bound for the population payoff's complete joint gradient.

Domain
Positive real number

$\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le\beta\|z-w\|_2$

$d$

The joint Euclidean dimension is $d=d_x+d_y$. Within its stated window, the lower bound may choose finite block dimensions.

Domain
Integer at least $2$
$\varepsilon$

This is the tangent-residual tolerance. The mean-square guarantee uses its square $\varepsilon^2$.

Domain
Positive real number
$\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$

Euclidean norm and inner product; the product-space norm is the square root of the sum of the squared block norms.

Domain
The specified finite-dimensional real vector space.

$\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$

$d_x,d_y$

Positive integer primal and dual block dimensions; joint dimension $d=d_x+d_y$

Domain
Positive integer
$f$

Unknown real-valued payoff, with primal and dual input blocks.

Domain
$f:(x,y)\mapsto f(x,y)\in\mathbb R$
$x,y,z$

Primal variable, dual variable, and joint point

Domain
$x\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ y\in\mathbb R^{d_y},\ z=(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}$

$z=(x,y)$

$\nabla f,\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f$

Complete joint gradient and its two blocks

Domain
$\nabla_x f\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\ \nabla_y f\in\mathbb R^{d_y}$

$\nabla f=(\nabla_x f,\nabla_y f)$

$\Phi$

Reduced objective after global dual maximization; neither its value nor gradient is an additional free interface

Domain
Real-valued function on the primal-variable space

$\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$

$X,Y$

The primal domain is known, nonempty, closed, and convex; the dual domain is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(Y)\le D_y$.

Domain
$X\subset\mathbb R^{d_x},\ Y\subset\mathbb R^{d_y}$
$N_K(z)$

Use the Euclidean normal cone of the closed convex feasible set K at the feasible point z. The same definition applies blockwise to $N_X$ and $N_Y$.

Domain
$z\in K,\quad N_K(z)\subset\mathbb R^d$

$N_K(z)=\{v:\langle v,u-z\rangle\le0\ \forall u\in K\}$

$\operatorname{dist}(0,S)$

Infimum of the Euclidean distances from vectors in $S$ to the origin

Domain
Nonnegative extended real value

$\operatorname{dist}(0,S)=\inf_{v\in S}\|v\|_2$

$x_0,y_0$

The public initial primal and dual variables.

Domain
The respective feasible domains. Both equal zero when the origins are explicitly fixed.
$\widehat x,\widehat y$

The point or variable blocks ultimately returned by the algorithm, corresponding to the hatted variables in the error formula.

Domain
Feasible variable pairs in $\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_y}$
$N_{\rm first}$

Number of bundled function-value and full joint-gradient queries

Domain
Nonnegative integer count; expected work is its expectation.
$N_{\rm projection}$

Projection count, uncharged in the primary query-cost projection

Domain
Nonnegative integer count; expected work is its expectation.
$N$

A uniform cap on principal information calls for every admissible instance and execution path.

Domain
Nonnegative integer
$N^\star$

The infimum principal query budget among algorithms satisfying every stated instancewise output guarantee.

Domain
Nonnegative extended real value; by convention, positive infinity if no successful algorithm or no uniform finite budget exists
$\mathcal A,I$

An algorithm selected from public inputs and an admissible hidden instance fixed before interaction

Domain
The specified algorithm and model classes.
$O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde O$

Asymptotic upper and lower bounds, constant-factor matching, and upper bounds hiding the stated logarithmic factors, within the corresponding regions.

Domain
Nonnegative complexity function; subscript p permits additional dependence only on fixed p
$\mathfrak A_\varepsilon$

Algorithms using the allowed interfaces, algorithm restrictions, and output domain, and satisfying the displayed complete error guarantee for every fixed admissible instance

Domain
The algorithm class is defined at fixed public parameters and target tolerance $\varepsilon$.

Compared quantities and resource definitions

Q1 · source scoped metric resource statement

Metric contract
output: domain: (xhat,yhat) in X x Y; postprocessing: arbitrary measurable transcript-based output unless algorithm restriction expressly states otherwise; metric: max{dist(0,grad_x f(xhat,yhat)+N_X(xhat)),dist(0,-grad_y f(xhat,yhat)+N_Y(yhat))}; guarantee: max{dist(0,grad_x f(xhat,yhat)+N_X(xhat)),dist(0,-grad_y f(xhat,yhat)+N_Y(yhat))}<=epsilon for every legal instance
Resource contract
budget: fixed worst-case cap on every transcript; primary: N_payoff_first_order; unit: one declared oracle call; auxiliary: projection/internal model solves separately retained, never counted as hidden oracle

This is the native source metric/resource guarantee. Joint precision, block size, runtime and oracle components stay separate; do not infer a scalar optimal query complexity.
